settings.finalizedWarning: Registration is finalized — changing the MacMahon groups will change everyone's points and future pairings.
settings.exportSettingsDesc: Download these settings as a JSON file — e.g. to compare pairing variants with the simulation tool.
settings.pairingModeMixedEloDesc: Keeps MacMahon and the Swiss score-group rules (score gap, float repeat, club protection, airtight groups), but replaces fold and floater selection with a live Bayesian ELO estimate, so pairing within (and across) a score group follows current form rather than the registration rating. Fully compatible with MacMahon points.
settings.eloModeDesc: Ignore Swiss / MacMahon entirely and pair each round to minimise the ELO difference of every game, using a live Bayesian estimate of each player's strength that updates from the results.
settings.eloDriftDesc: How fast an estimate may drift from the registration rating (applied to each player's FESA K factor). 1 keeps ratings close; higher reacts faster to upsets. Usually 1–4.
settings.eloProvisionalDesc: Extra drift for players whose rating is less trustworthy — not found in the FESA list (rating typed by hand) or with fewer than 18 FESA games. Applied on top of the multiplier above; 1 disables it.
settings.eloUnratedDesc: The prior for an unrated player: where their estimate starts (center) and how loose it is, as a K on the same scale as a rated player's FESA K (a rated K is ~16–40; the unrated default 705 gives roughly the same spread as ±350 ELO). Bigger K lets results move the estimate faster.
settings.eloPriorShapeDesc: Shape of the prior for unrated players only (rated players always use the Gaussian). Gaussian pulls the estimate back to the prior centre ever harder the further it drifts (a single result is capped near the player's K). Laplace has a constant pull and fatter tails, so an unrated newcomer who keeps beating the field climbs much further toward their true strength — the case that matters for strong veterans arriving without an ELO. Flat uses no prior at all: the rating is the pure performance rating over the games, exactly as the FESA rating program computes it for newcomers (an all-loss newcomer floors to 1, an all-win one is rated as if they had drawn their strongest opponent). Gaussian and Laplace can be made asymmetric with the looseness knobs below; Flat has no arm to widen.
settings.eloUpwardLoosenessDesc: How much easier it is to revise a player's estimate up than down — the common case being an under-rated improver. Applies to either prior shape. 1 is symmetric; higher lets an upward correction clear on less evidence, while a downward one stays as tight as before. Set separately per player category, since a reliable rating deserves less upward tilt than a newcomer.
settings.eloEstimateKnobsMacmahonNote: These tune the ELO estimate used to award MacMahon points.
settings.macmahonDesc: Each player starts with one point per threshold they reach — an ELO rating or a dan/kyu grade. For example, with thresholds 1200 ELO and 1700 ELO a player rated below 1200 starts at 0, from 1200 to 1699 at 1, and 1700 or above at 2; a grade threshold works the same way on a player's dan/kyu grade instead. ELO and grade thresholds are independent — a player is scored on each axis it configures. A player missing the value a threshold needs (no rating, no grade) never meets it. Leave the list empty to disable MacMahon.
settings.noThresholds: No thresholds — every player starts at 0 MacMahon points.
settings.degressiveDesc: Check “stops after round” on a threshold to drop it once that round is complete, so the starting-point head start fades as the field converges. Each threshold can be given its own stopping round.
settings.airtightGroupsDesc: For the first N rounds, an extra rule (just below no-rematch, above equal-scores) avoids pairing players with a different number of MacMahon points — penalty grows with the square of the gap, like the other gap rules. Off by default.
settings.macmahonFromEloDesc: Award MacMahon starting points from a live ELO estimate rather than each player's registration rating: every ELO threshold is compared against the same Bayesian estimate used by the ELO pairing modes, recomputed each round, so a player's starting points can rise or fall as their estimated strength moves. Grade thresholds are unaffected. Works with plain Swiss or mixed-ELO pairing. Off by default.
settings.macmahonFromEloCheckbox: Award MacMahon from the estimated ELO
settings.macmahonFromEloNeedsEloThreshold: Add at least one ELO threshold above to enable this.
settings.clubProtectionDesc: Avoid pairing players from the same club. Off by default. Club names are matched case-insensitively; players with no club set are never protected.
settings.clubProtectionCheckbox: Avoid pairing players from the same club
settings.exemptDesc: Clubs exempt from protection — their members may still be paired (e.g. the host club, whose entrants are expected to meet):
settings.noExemptions: No exemptions — every club is protected.
settings.floaterDesc: When a score group has to pair across groups, who floats? The weakest of the upper group always drops down; this chooses who the lower group sends up.
settings.floaterClassic: Classic Swiss — the strongest of the lower group floats up
settings.floaterMedian: Median Swiss — the median of the lower group floats up
settings.hybridCupDesc: Run a direct-elimination cup among the top eligible players alongside the Swiss (the French / European Championship format). Enabling this adds an eligibility column to registration; you pick the bracket size (top 8/16/32/64) when you finalize registration.
settings.hybridCupCheckbox: Hybrid tournament with a direct-elimination cup
settings.handicapDesc: Controls the handicap column(s) in the pairings view. A recommended handicap (FFS Annexe 7, from the rating gap) is highlighted in the picker whenever it's shown, whichever option is chosen below. Cup games never have a handicap.
settings.handicapNone: No handicap games — hide the column
settings.handicapAllowed: Handicap games allowed — show the picker
settings.handicapSuggested: Handicap games suggested — also show a suggested-handicap column
settings.handicapWielCheckbox: "Wiel" rule: the giver always counts as the winner
settings.handicapWielDesc: When on, a handicap game always credits the giver as the winner in the standings and for pairing, whatever the actual result. When off (the default), handicap games score like any other game.
settings.rankingDesc: Players are ranked by these criteria in order (the tournament number breaks anything still level), and only these columns appear on the Standings tab. Points is one of them — normally first, but you can reorder it like the rest. Each opponent-sum metric comes in a MacMahon-inclusive (M) and a wins-only (W) flavour.
settings.noTiebreaks: No tie-breaks — players level on points are ordered by tournament number.
